findings.text: The first paragraph tells a newcomer what Athena is, who it is for and what problem it solves, in plain words. They can answer "what is this?" before they scroll.
findings.source: header lede: "Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository... It solves the problem of AI edits that arrive unreviewed and unaccountable."

findings.text: The top of the page links to a Next steps section that lists prerequisites, a clone command, ./setup.sh and a first command to try. A newcomer knows what to do next.
findings.source: header: "Next step: install Athena or read firstmate itself" and Next steps: "Try it with a one-line request: athena ask "add a changelog""

findings.text: The second section, which should be the evidence that Athena works, shows an internal error message. The lede promises a commit traced to models, cost and verdict, and this is the only place the page could show one. A newcomer sees a broken demo early and has reason to doubt the rest.
findings.source: Check it on a real job: "The records of job 20261029-073603-7kqv could not be read here, so no models, verdict or costs are shown: no reading record for job 20261029-073603-7kqv."

findings.text: On Athena's own site, the title is about a different project, firstmate. A newcomer who expects a page about Athena may think they have landed in the wrong place until they read the second lede paragraph.
findings.source: <title>Athena explains how firstmate handles work</title> and the h1 of the same text

findings.text: This link speaks to the page owner, not to a visitor, and it sits beside the newcomer's next-step link. It is unclear whose decisions are meant, which makes it confusing to a first-time reader.
findings.source: header: "Owner view: proposals waiting for your decision."

findings.text: Most of the page is a dense state machine of firstmate's internals: 12 transition cards, 45 claims, and terms such as yolo, captain call and places-held. It does show that Athena traces every claim to source lines, but a newcomer who wants to judge Athena has to infer the value from volume instead of being shown one short worked example.
findings.source: Sections Transitions, Why it is built this way, Glossary, Claims and sources

findings.text: Several key terms are honestly marked as undefined in the source. That is trustworthy, but it leaves gaps in the firstmate walkthrough that a newcomer cannot fill.
findings.source: Glossary: "captain call — The firstmate source does not define a captain call." and in scope: "this page gives no test for it"

findings.text: The same definitions (yolo, in scope, green, red, home) appear twice, once near the top and again in the Glossary. This makes an already long page longer without adding anything for the reader.
This explains an internal repository folder that a newcomer has no context for and no use for.
findings.source: About this page: "the name of the folder under studies/ that holds the data this page is generated from"
